{
  "title": "The Keeper's Light",
  "world": "cinematic storybook realism — tactile, believable, gentle wonder",
  "cold_open": "Storms howled over the cliffs, but the old lighthouse still burned, as if waiting for someone to return.",
  "question": "Why did the lamp light itself, years after its keeper died?",
  "journey": "A boy named Elias climbed the winding stairs of the lighthouse, lantern in hand. He had heard stories of the keeper who vanished on a storm night long ago. The air was thick with salt and memory. Every step echoed, as though the walls remembered the man who once walked them. He reached the top, where the great lens stood dark and silent, waiting.",
  "discovery": "Elias found a pocket watch, its glass cracked. Inside, a faded photo of the keeper, smiling, holding a child. The watch still ticked, though it should have stopped years ago.",
  "emotional_turn": "Tears blurred the photo as Elias realized the keeper had once been his grandfather, lost to time and tide. The light had never truly gone out—it had been waiting for him.",
  "payoff": "As Elias turned the watch, the lens flared to life, casting golden light across the stormy sea, as if the past and present had finally met.",
  "after_image": "The boy stood alone, bathed in light.",
  "hero_shot": "The lighthouse beam cuts through the storm, revealing a boat with a single figure, waving."
}
